title: Numbers Chapter 31 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Numbers chapter 31 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Numbers Chapter 31 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Numbers Chapter 31.

questions.question: Who spoke to Moses commanding him to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The LORD spoke unto Moses instructing him to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites as stated in Numbers 31:1.

questions.question: What was Moses told would happen to him after avenging the Midianites?
options: He would be gathered unto his people
He would become king of Israel
He would lead the army again
He would enter the Promised Land
questions.correctAnswer: He would be gathered unto his people
questions.explanation: The LORD told Moses he would be gathered unto his people after avenging the children of Israel of the Midianites in Numbers 31:2.

questions.question: How many men from each tribe were to be sent to war against the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: One thousand
questions.explanation: Moses commanded that a thousand men from every tribe be sent to war against the Midianites in Numbers 31:4.

questions.question: How many men in total were armed for war from all the tribes of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve thousand
questions.explanation: There were twelve thousand men armed for war, a thousand from each of the twelve tribes of Israel as stated in Numbers 31:5.

questions.question: Who accompanied the men to war along with the holy instruments and trumpets?
options: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
questions.correctAnswer: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest
questions.explanation: Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest was sent with the men to war, carrying the holy instruments and trumpets as stated in Numbers 31:6.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do to the males of the Midianites in battle?
options: They made a treaty with them
questions.correctAnswer: They slew all the males
questions.explanation: The Israelites slew all the males of the Midianites as commanded by the LORD in Numbers 31:7.

questions.question: How many kings of Midian were slain, and can you name one?
questions.correctAnswer: Five kings, including Evi
questions.explanation: Five kings of Midian were slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, as recorded in Numbers 31:8.

questions.question: True or False: Balaam the son of Beor was spared by the Israelites.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Balaam the son of Beor was slain with the sword by the Israelites as stated in Numbers 31:8.

questions.question: What did the children of Israel do with the women and little ones of Midian?
questions.correctAnswer: Took them captives
questions.explanation: The children of Israel took all the women of Midian captives, along with their little ones, as stated in Numbers 31:9.

questions.question: What did the Israelites do to the cities and castles of Midian?
options: Burnt all their cities and castles with fire
questions.correctAnswer: Burnt all their cities and castles with fire
questions.explanation: They burnt all the cities and goodly castles of Midian with fire as commanded in Numbers 31:10.

questions.question: Where did the Israelites bring the captives, prey, and spoil from the battle?
options: To the camp at the plains of Moab
questions.correctAnswer: To the camp at the plains of Moab
questions.explanation: They brought the captives and spoil unto Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation at the camp in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho as stated in Numbers 31:12.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was pleased with the officers of the host when they returned from battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Moses was wroth with the officers of the host when they came from battle as recorded in Numbers 31:14.

questions.question: What question did Moses ask the officers about the women taken from Midian?
options: Have ye saved all the women alive?
Have ye killed all the women?
Have ye taken the women captive?
Have ye given the women gifts?
questions.correctAnswer: Have ye saved all the women alive?
questions.explanation: Moses asked the officers if they had saved all the women alive as stated in Numbers 31:15.

questions.question: What caused the children of Israel to trespass against the LORD in the matter of Peor?
questions.correctAnswer: The counsel of Balaam
questions.explanation: The women caused Israel to sin through the counsel of Balaam, leading to a plague among the congregation, as explained in Numbers 31:16.

questions.question: According to Moses' command, which women should be kept alive?
options: Women children that have not known a man by lying with him
questions.correctAnswer: Women children that have not known a man by lying with him
questions.explanation: Moses commanded to keep alive all the women children that have not known a man by lying with him, as stated in Numbers 31:18.

medium.title: Numbers Chapter 31 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Numbers Chapter 31 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Numbers 31:19, how long were the Israelites commanded to remain outside the camp for purification?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven days
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:19 instructs the Israelites to abide outside the camp for seven days for purification after contact with the slain.

questions.question: What are the Israelites instructed to purify along with themselves on the third and seventh days, according to Numbers 31:19?
questions.correctAnswer: Their captives as well
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:19 commands purification of both the individuals who killed or touched the slain and their captives on the third and seventh days.

questions.question: Numbers 31:20 lists items to be purified. Which of the following is NOT explicitly mentioned as needing purification?
questions.correctAnswer: Stone utensils
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:20 specifies raiment, things made of wood, and goats' hair works but does not mention stone utensils for purification.

questions.question: In Numbers 31:21, Eleazar the priest tells the men of war that the purification ordinance was commanded by whom?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:21 records Eleazar saying this is the ordinance of the law which the LORD commanded Moses, emphasizing divine authority.

questions.question: Which metals are mentioned in Numbers 31:22 as subject to purification by fire?
options: Gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead
Gold, copper, bronze, silver, iron, and tin
Silver, brass, lead, tin, iron, and bronze
Gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, and bronze
questions.correctAnswer: Gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:22 lists gold, silver, brass, iron, tin, and lead as metals to be purified by fire.

questions.question: According to Numbers 31:23, what must be done to objects that cannot endure fire for purification?
options: They must be purified with water
questions.correctAnswer: They must be purified with water
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:23 explains that items not able to endure fire must be purified with water of separation, while those that endure fire go through fire and water.

questions.question: What does Numbers 31:24 say will happen after washing clothes on the seventh day?
options: They shall be clean and may enter the camp
They shall remain outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be clean and may enter the camp
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:24 states that washing clothes on the seventh day results in being clean and able to enter the camp.

questions.question: In Numbers 31:26-27, what two groups is the spoil divided between?
options: The men who went to battle and the whole congregation
The elders and the young men
questions.correctAnswer: The men who went to battle and the whole congregation
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:26-27 commands dividing the spoil between the men who went to war and the entire congregation.

questions.question: What is the ratio of tribute to the LORD from the men who went to war as stated in Numbers 31:28?
questions.correctAnswer: One soul of five hundred
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:28 states the tribute to the LORD is one soul of five hundred from the men of war, including persons and animals.

questions.question: Based on Numbers 31:29-30, who receives the tribute taken from the congregation's half of the spoil?
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:30 specifies that one portion of fifty from the congregation’s half is given to the Levites, who keep the tabernacle.

questions.question: According to Numbers 31:32-35, approximately how many women who had not known a man were taken captive?
questions.correctAnswer: Thirty-two thousand
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:35 records thirty-two thousand women who had not known a man were taken captive.

questions.question: What does Numbers 31:36 reveal about the portion of the spoil belonging to the men who went to war?
options: It was half the total spoil
It was a quarter of the spoil
questions.correctAnswer: It was half the total spoil
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:36 states the half which was the portion of the men who went to war consisted of specific numbers of sheep, indicating half the total spoil.

questions.question: True or False: According to Numbers 31:24, washing clothes on the seventh day makes the people clean and allows them to enter the camp.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:24 clearly states washing clothes on the seventh day results in being clean and permits entry into the camp.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 31:23 teaches that all items, regardless of their material, must be purified by fire.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:23 explains that only items that can endure fire are purified by fire; others must be purified by water, so not all items are burned.

questions.question: True or False: Numbers 31:28-29 instructs that the tribute to the LORD should be taken from the half of the spoil belonging to the men who fought in the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:28-29 states the tribute of one soul of five hundred is taken from the half belonging to the men who went to battle and given to Eleazar the priest.

hard.title: Numbers Chapter 31 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Numbers Chapter 31.

questions.question: How many sheep were included in the LORD's tribute from the spoils taken in the battle against Midian?
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:37 states the LORD'S tribute of the sheep was six hundred and threescore and fifteen, which equals 675.

questions.question: What was the number of beeves taken in the spoil, and how many of these were given as the LORD's tribute?
questions.correctAnswer: 36,000 beeves; 72 tribute
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:38 records thirty-six thousand beeves were taken, and the LORD'S tribute of them was seventy-two.

questions.question: What was the total number of asses taken, and how many were allocated as the LORD's tribute?
questions.correctAnswer: 30,500 asses; 61 tribute
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:39 states thirty thousand and five hundred asses were taken, with sixty-one given as the LORD'S tribute.

questions.question: How many persons were taken, and how many of them were given as the LORD's tribute?
questions.correctAnswer: 16,000 persons; 32 tribute
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:40 records sixteen thousand persons taken, with thirty-two given as the LORD'S tribute.

questions.question: To whom did Moses give the LORD’s heave offering (tribute) after the battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Eleazar the priest
questions.explanation: According to Numbers 31:41, Moses gave the tribute, the LORD’S heave offering, to Eleazar the priest as commanded.

questions.question: What portion of the spoils did Moses give to the Levites who kept the charge of the tabernacle?
options: One portion of fifty from the children of Israel's half
One fifth of the entire spoil
One tenth of the spoils taken by the men of war
All the gold and silver spoils
questions.correctAnswer: One portion of fifty from the children of Israel's half
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:30 and Numbers 31:47 indicate Moses took one portion of fifty from the children of Israel's half and gave it to the Levites.

questions.question: How did the officers report to Moses about the men of war under their charge?
options: They accounted for all men; none were missing
They reported several men lost in battle
They requested reinforcements due to heavy losses
They reported all men were wounded
questions.correctAnswer: They accounted for all men; none were missing
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:49 shows the officers told Moses that none of the men under their charge were missing.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the oblation the officers brought to the LORD?
options: To make an atonement for their souls
To celebrate the victory with a feast
To pay the priests for their services
questions.correctAnswer: To make an atonement for their souls
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:50 explains the officers brought an oblation to make an atonement for their souls before the LORD.

questions.question: How much gold was offered by the captains of thousands and hundreds as an offering unto the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: 16,750 shekels
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:52 records the total gold offering was sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels.

questions.question: What did Moses and Eleazar do with the gold of the captains of thousands and hundreds?
options: Brought it into the tabernacle of the congregation for a memorial
Used it to pay the soldiers
Gave it to the Levites for upkeep
Buried it as a hidden treasure
questions.correctAnswer: Brought it into the tabernacle of the congregation for a memorial
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:54 states Moses and Eleazar took the gold and brought it into the tabernacle for a memorial before the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The number of sheep taken by the men of war was more than 300,000.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:43 specifies that the half belonging to the congregation was over three hundred thousand sheep, indicating a very large number taken.

questions.question: True or False: The tribute given to the Levites was taken from the spoils belonging to the men who went to war.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:30 and 31:47 clarify that the Levites’ portion was taken from the children of Israel's half, not from the men who went to war.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of giving a tribute or offering to the LORD from spoils or possessions?
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 27:30
questions.explanation: Leviticus 27:30 discusses tithes and offerings given to the LORD, paralleling the tribute to the LORD in Numbers 31:37-40.

questions.question: What Hebrew word meaning 'heave offering' is significant in this chapter and what does it imply about the nature of the tribute?
options: Terumah, implying a lifted or elevated gift
questions.correctAnswer: Terumah, implying a lifted or elevated gift
questions.explanation: 'Heave offering' in Numbers 31:41 is translated from the Hebrew 'Terumah,' denoting a gift lifted up to the LORD as holy.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified by the division of the spoils into halves and further portions for priests and Levites in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiastic structure highlighting sacred order
questions.explanation: The structured division of spoils in Numbers 31:26-47 shows a chiastic pattern emphasizing the sacred distribution between warriors, congregation, priests, and Levites.

theological.title: Numbers Chapter 31 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Numbers Chapter 31 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by God's command to Moses to avenge Israel against Midian before Moses himself dies?
options: God's justice and faithfulness to His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and faithfulness to His covenant
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:2 shows God's justice in commanding vengeance against Midian and His faithfulness in fulfilling His promises to Israel, even as Moses is told he will soon die.

questions.question: According to Numbers 31:4-6, what does the methodical sending of a thousand armed men from each tribe reveal about Israel's approach to warfare?
options: It reflects God's orderliness and organized execution of His commands
It shows the tribes competed for glory in battle
It indicates reliance on human strength alone
It was a spontaneous, unplanned attack
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects God's orderliness and organized execution of His commands
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:4-6 describes a precise and organized military mobilization under God's command, demonstrating divine orderliness in Israel's warfare.

questions.question: What theological significance does the killing of Balaam alongside the Midianite kings have in this chapter’s narrative?
options: It symbolizes the removal of corrupt prophetic influence that led Israel to sin
It shows the defeat of political enemies only
It represents God’s rejection of all foreigners
It was an act of revenge without theological meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the removal of corrupt prophetic influence that led Israel to sin
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:8 includes Balaam’s death, underscoring the judgment on the false prophet who counseled Israel’s sin at Peor, thus purging evil influence.

questions.question: How does the command to kill all males and women who have known a man, but to keep virgin women alive, reflect Israel’s sanctification process in Numbers 31?
options: It emphasizes ritual purity and separation from idolatry
It shows indiscriminate violence without reason
It indicates a tolerance for all cultures
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes ritual purity and separation from idolatry
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:17-18 commands selective killing to prevent contamination from Midianite idolatry, preserving purity among Israel by separating from sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about communal holiness is reflected in the instruction to purify both the soldiers and captives on the third and seventh days after battle?
options: The doctrine of ceremonial cleansing and sanctification
The doctrine of justification by faith alone
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of ceremonial cleansing and sanctification
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:19-20 prescribes purification rituals, teaching the necessity of holiness and sanctification after contact with death and sin.

questions.question: How does the detailed division and tribute of the spoils between the warriors and the congregation illustrate God's justice and provision?
options: God's equitable sharing of blessings and acknowledgment of service
God's favoritism toward the priests only
God's exclusive focus on material wealth
questions.correctAnswer: God's equitable sharing of blessings and acknowledgment of service
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:26-30 shows God’s just distribution of spoils, rewarding warriors and the whole congregation fairly, highlighting His provision and fairness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the violence commanded in Numbers 31 condones cruelty. What does Numbers 31:14-18 actually teach about God's judgment and holiness?
options: God’s judgment is purposeful to remove sin and maintain His holy covenant community
God arbitrarily punishes enemies without cause
God is indifferent to sin and its consequences
God favors violent conquest over mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is purposeful to remove sin and maintain His holy covenant community
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:14-18 explains that the violence was an act of holy judgment to prevent Israel’s contamination through Midianite sin, showing God’s holiness and justice.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's holiness and Israel’s obedience is conveyed by the instructions in Numbers 31:19-24 concerning purification after battle?
options: God requires ritual purity as a sign of holiness and Israel must obey His ordinances
God allows Israel to remain unclean after battle
God's laws are flexible and optional
God only cares about moral purity, not ceremonial
questions.correctAnswer: God requires ritual purity as a sign of holiness and Israel must obey His ordinances
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:19-24 combines God's demand for purification rituals with Israel’s obedience, teaching sanctification requires both moral and ceremonial cleansing.

questions.question: How does the presence of Eleazar the priest among the warriors in Numbers 31:6 and later in the division of spoils reflect the role of the priesthood in Israel's covenant community?
options: The priesthood mediates God's holiness and oversees covenant obedience
The priesthood is merely ceremonial without real authority
The priesthood commands the army in battle
The priesthood acts as political rulers
questions.correctAnswer: The priesthood mediates God's holiness and oversees covenant obedience
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:6 and 31:26 show Eleazar as a spiritual mediator, ensuring God’s laws are followed in war and distribution, reflecting priestly responsibility in covenant life.

questions.question: What does the large number of spoils listed in Numbers 31:32-35 teach about God's blessing and provision following obedience to His commands?
options: God abundantly blesses those who obey His righteous commands
God limits blessings to spiritual gifts only
Spoils are irrelevant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God abundantly blesses those who obey His righteous commands
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:32-35 details vast spoils, showing God’s abundant provision as a reward for Israel’s obedience in carrying out divine judgment.

questions.question: What is revealed about God's attribute of holiness in the requirement to separate the gold and metals and purify them by fire in Numbers 31:22-23?
options: God’s holiness demands purification and consecration of all that is dedicated to Him
God does not care about material purity
God's holiness is only about moral behavior
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness demands purification and consecration of all that is dedicated to Him
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:22-23 teaches that even precious metals must be purified by fire to be holy and acceptable to God, reflecting His absolute holiness.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about the role of the Levites is taught by the command to give them a portion of the spoils for keeping the charge of the tabernacle (Numbers 31:30, 47)?
options: The Levites serve as mediators and caretakers of God's presence, supported by the community
The Levites are warriors with no religious duties
The Levites receive spoils to become wealthy
The Levites are excluded from blessings
questions.correctAnswer: The Levites serve as mediators and caretakers of God's presence, supported by the community
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:30 and 47 teach that Levites receive a portion as support for their spiritual service, underscoring their mediatory role in Israel’s worship.

questions.question: How does the response of the officers bringing a gold offering to Moses (Numbers 31:49-52) illustrate Israel's acknowledgment of divine sovereignty over victory?
options: It shows their recognition of God’s providence and their need for atonement
It reveals pride in human military power
It demonstrates a rejection of God
questions.correctAnswer: It shows their recognition of God’s providence and their need for atonement
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:49-52 records the officers offering gold to the LORD as an atonement, acknowledging God’s sovereignty in giving them victory.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Numbers 31:7-8 and 31:16 provide about sin, judgment, and the consequences of leading others into idolatry?
options: Sin leads to divine judgment not only on the sinner but also on those influenced, as shown by the destruction of Midianites and Balaam
Judgment is random and unrelated to sin
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to divine judgment not only on the sinner but also on those influenced, as shown by the destruction of Midianites and Balaam
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:7-8 and 31:16 show that sin, especially through false counsel like Balaam's, results in God's judgment on offenders and those they lead into sin.

questions.question: How does Numbers 31:25-30 teach about God’s requirement for holiness in both material possessions and personal conduct?
options: God commands purification and proper distribution of both spoils and people to maintain holiness
God does not concern Himself with material things
Only personal conduct matters, not possessions
Material possessions are irrelevant to holiness
questions.correctAnswer: God commands purification and proper distribution of both spoils and people to maintain holiness
questions.explanation: Numbers 31:25-30 details purification rituals and the division of spoils, teaching that holiness encompasses both persons and possessions.
